mainEntity.name: Is software built with AI less reliable or lower quality than software built by humans?

acceptedAnswer.text:
AI assistance does not automatically make software lower quality, but quality depends on the workflow around it. Clear specifications, small changes, testing, review, documentation, and maintainable dependencies matter more than whether a person or model typed each line.

The main risk is accepting code that no one fully understands. That risk is higher when an owner treats a prototype as finished software or adds features without measuring whether they solve a real customer problem.

Key factors:
- Clarity of requirements.
- Reviewability of each change.
- Test and monitoring coverage.
- Long-term maintainability and ownership.

Practical guidance: Keep changes small enough to explain, require a code review, and document why important design choices were made. For a business prototype, label experimental features clearly and avoid promising reliability before real testing.

Run My AI Business frames AI-created workflows as educational starting points, not guaranteed outcomes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not automatically. Reliability depends on requirements, review, testing, security, documentation, and maintenance. AI-generated code becomes risky when nobody understands it or when a prototype is treated as finished software without validating real user behavior.
